comparison: Perfect agreement on NGR1-GFP localization data (C8-C16). Both evaluations find the microscopy evidence compelling and support the functional validation through phenotypic rescue. Peer reviewers specifically praise the 'compelling molecular and cell biological data' with no concerns raised.

Perfect agreement on BFA experiments (C35-C39, C84). Both evaluations support the finding that NGR1-GFP behavior is distinct from PIN proteins and not dependent on BFA-sensitive trafficking. Peer reviewers highlight this as a key distinguishing feature with no concerns.

Agreement on citation of concurrent publications (C92-C93). Both acknowledge the complementary work by Nishimura et al. and Chen et al. However, peer reviewers note the discussion could be more comprehensive in integrating these concurrent findings.

Strong agreement on pharmacological experiments (C40-C49, C94). Both evaluations support the findings showing NGR1-GFP sensitivity to sterol and PI4K inhibitors. OpenEval emphasizes the systematic approach and controls; peer reviewers describe findings as 'striking' with no methodological concerns.

Divergent evaluations of the integrated model (C115-C119). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the model is plausible but key mechanistic links remain unproven. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, emphasizing how the work 'bridges this critical knowledge gap' without raising concerns about speculative elements.

Agreement on D6PK findings (C71-C76, C100). Both evaluations strongly support the evidence for NGR-dependent D6PK relocalization. Peer reviewers emphasize this as 'really compelling' and a key contribution. OpenEval highlights the cell-type specificity as particularly strong evidence.

Partial overlap on mutagenesis experiments (C50-C62, C69-C70). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with systematic demonstration of synergistic requirements. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN due to incomplete statistical reporting in supplementary figures, specifically noting missing n values, statistical lettering, and p-values in Figs. 3F, 3D, and S3D.

Divergent evaluations of temporal dynamics (C17-C22, C30). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on time-lapse microscopy showing coordinated NGR1 movement with statoliths. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, requesting additional images at key time-points to visually document dynamics of PIN3, calcium, and auxin reporter; authors declined citing space concerns.

Partial overlap on rescue experiments (C63-C68, C87-C91). OpenEval strongly supports the evidence that alternative membrane anchors restore function. This overlaps with peer review R5 which covers broader mutagenesis claims but rates as UNCERTAIN due to statistical reporting issues in supplementary figures.

Partial overlap on PIN3 dynamics (C26-C29, C33). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting the paradox of late visible polarization but early functional requirement motivates the D6PK investigation. Peer reviewers rate the broader temporal dynamics as UNCERTAIN, requesting additional visual documentation at key time-points.

Partial overlap on calcium imaging (C23-C25, C31-C32, C78-C81). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with strong temporal resolution data. Peer reviewers include calcium dynamics in their UNCERTAIN evaluation, requesting specific images at key time-points to complement the graphical data in panel E.

OpenEval evaluates D6PK temporal dynamics and negative feedback speculation (C113-C114) as SUPPORTED for observations but notes feedback mechanism is speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.
OpenEval evaluates background/established knowledge claims (C1-C7) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these foundational claims.
OpenEval evaluates literature citations for D6PK context (C102-C112) as SUPPORTED with appropriate references. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these citation claims.
OpenEval evaluates literature citations on membrane composition and PIN behavior (C95-C98) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific citation claims.
OpenEval evaluates comprehensive background knowledge claims (C120-C133) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these foundational claims.
OpenEval evaluates citation of recent work on early root bending (C83) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific citation claim.

Peer reviewers provide overall positive evaluation of the integrated model and how it advances understanding of gravity sensing. This appears to be a holistic assessment rather than evaluation of specific mechanistic claims, though it overlaps with OpenEval R10 on model claims C115-C119.
